questions.question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

CHRONIC
questions.solution:
The meanings of the given words are as follows:

*__**chronic: constantly recurring or (of an illness) persisting for a long time**__*

 
• *__continuing__*: without a break in continuity.
 
• *__infrequent__*: not occurring often.
 
• *__routine__*: a sequence of actions regularly followed.
 
• *__regular__*: recurring at uniform intervals.

Clearly, **'chronic'** and **'infrequent'** are words with **opposite** meanings.(**antonyms**)

Thus, option **2 **is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.

The express bus __generally stops at only the major town__s on the route.

options.text: generally stop in only the major towns
generally stopped from only the major towns
generally stopping on only the major towns

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4) i.e. No improvement.**

 
• The given sentence is a **routine action** and the tense used for routine action is the **present indefinite tense.**
 
• The subject in the sentence is **singular** i.e. bus, hence the **verb** used also be **singular**, so, the usage of the verb **'stops'** is correct.
 
• Hence, the given sentence is grammatically correct and needs no improvement.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.

__If I does not pay__ my post-paid mobile bill by tomorrow I will probably have to pay a fine.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3) i.e. If I do not pay.**

 
• The given sentence is a **conditional sentence**, hence, the first action should be in the present **indefinite tense** and the second sentence will be in the **future indefinite tense**.
 
• And in the present indefinite tense, if the subject is 'I' the helping verb i.e. do does not take **'s/es'** with it.
 
• So,** 'do not' **will be used in place of **'does not'**.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.**1.**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2) i.e. it.**

 
• In the given blank we need a pronoun to be used in place of **'the given sentence'**. 
 
• And the sentence is a** non-living thing** and singular.
 
• Hence, **'it'** will be used as a **pronoun** in the given blank.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.**2.**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3) i.e. have.**

 
• The given sentence is in **present tense**, so, option 1) i.e. **'had**' cannot be used here.
 
• And the subject is plural in the given sentence i.e. **'we'**, hence, the verb will also be plural i.e. have.
 
• Because 'has' is used for singular subjects and 'have' is used for plural subjects.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.**3.**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4) i.e. doesn't.**

 
• The given sentence implies that the subject does not have any pencils, hence, **'not'** will be used with the helping verb.
 
• And the subject is **singular** i.e. he, in the given sentence, hence, the helping verb will also be singular i.e. **does.**
 
• So, the correct word to fill in the given blank is **'doesn't'**.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No**.4.**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4) i.e. do.**

 
• The given sentence is in **present indefinite tense**, hence, the helping verb that can be used here is **'do/does'**.
 
• The subject in the given sentence is **'you'** and it takes **'do'** as a helping verb with it. 
 
• So, the correct word to use in the blank is 'do'

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

They will not allow mobile phones in the examination hall.

options.text: Mobile phones will not be allowed in the examination hall.
Mobile phones were not allowed in the examination hall.
Mobile phones are not allowed in the examination hall.
Mobile phones are not being allowed in the examination hall.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1.

Future indefinite tense __**Active form**__- subject + will/shall + v1 + object + other words.

Future indefinite tense **__Passive form__**- object + will/shall + be + v3 + by + subject + other words.

Option 1 follows this rule so, the chosen option is correct.

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.

A. Today, man is master of the world and he makes the animals do what he likes.

B. Others he eats; and those like the lion and the tiger, he shoots for pleasure.

C. Early man, when he first came, must have been surrounded by many huge animals, and he must have lived in fear of them.

D. Some he tames like the horse, the cow, the elephant, the dog, the cat and so many others.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e. CADB.

As after reading one or two lines it can be said that this para jumble is talking about the evolution of man.

So, we must start this with the early life of a human on the earth.

Sentence C conveys this idea so, this should be the first sentence.

we have C at first position in options 2 and 4.

B & D are the sentences talking about today's man and sentence A is introducing the man today. So sentence A will follow sentence C.

Sentence B starts with others so it can not just after A as the use 'others' won't convey a clear meaning.

So we have only one choice now that Sentence D will follow sentence A and then B will come.

Thus, the correct order is CABD.

questions.question:
How many triangles are present in the following figure?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e1c77a36c3ad0b282a670a205a375c6c861902b60b192f93014c194f0a1717a8.png]
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6f8892e089b0d5df1e871c866f16f981559fb22699eaa488193ca1c9db59b445.png] 

When a triangle is divided in different bases, then count the number of triangles and add them all.

In triangle ABD, we have two bases = BC and CD ⇒ 3 triangles

In triangle BGD, we have two bases = GI and ID ⇒ 3 triangles

In triangle EGH, we have two bases = GF and FE ⇒ 3 triangles

The last triangle remaining is GED.

Thus, total triangles = 3 + 3 + 3 + 1 = 10

Hence, “10” is the correct answer.

questions.question: If RUBY is coded as 264 and PAY is coded as 126, then how will RUPAY be coded as?

The pattern followed here is:

Similarly,

RUPAY → 18 + 21 + 16 + 1 + 25 = 81 and 81 × 5 = 405 where 5 is the no. of letters in the word RUPAY.

Hence, 405 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All eggs are hens.

All hens are birds.

All birds are crows.

**Conclusions:**

I. All eggs are crows.

II. All hens are crows.

III. Some crows are birds.

options.text: Only conclusion I and II follow.
All conclusions I, II and III follow.
Only conclusion II and III follow.

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram is as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/81a868a1174f42829caa6a45f0e8e2f8bb18cfd87be66ccd1bf009982f3551ba.png] 

**Explanation:**

I. All eggs are crows → True (All eggs are hens, which are birds, which in turn are crows. So, all eggs are crows is true).

II. All hens are crows → True (All hens are birds, which are crows. So, all hens are crows is true).

III. Some crows are birds → True (All birds are crows. So, some part of crows will be birds)

Hence, “All conclusions I, II and III follow” is the correct answer.

questions.question: What will be the day of the week on 15 August 2021?
questions.solution:
Till 2000, odd days = 0 (2000 is a century leap year)

Odd days in 20 years (from 2001 to 2020) = (No. of leap years × 2 + no. of non-leap years × 1) mod 7 = (5 × 2 + 15 × 1) mod 7 = remainder of (25 ÷ 7) = 4

2021 is a non-leap year

Odd days in 2021 → (odd days in jan + odd days in feb + odd days in march + odd days in april + odd days in may + odd days in june + odd days in july + odd days till 15 august) mod 7

Odd days = 3 + 0 + 3 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 3 + 1 = 17 odd days = 17 ÷ 7 = 3 days

Total odd days = 4 odd days + 3 odd days = 7 odd days

Total odd days = 7 ÷ 7 = 0 (remainder) → 0 odd days

questions.question: By how much quantity is the average sale per month from B more or less than that from C?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

The total sale from B of all the months = 9000 + 7000 + 9000 + 11000 = 36000

The average sale from B of all the months = 36000/4 = 9000

The total sale from C of all the months = 10000 + 5000 + 8000 + 9000 = 32000

The average sale from C of all the months = 32000/4 = 8000 kg

Difference of the average sale from B and C = 9000 – 8000 = 1000 kg

**∴ The average sale per month from B is 1000 kg more than that from C**

questions.question: Arrange the ratio of sales from B to that from A and C, taken together, month wise in ascending order.
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Ratio of sales from B to that from A and C in Jan = 9/(8 + 10) = 9/18 = 0.5

Ratio of sales from B to that from A and C in Feb = 7/(6 + 5) = 7/11 = 0.63

questions.question: What is the ratio of rate of growth in sales from B to the rate of growth in sales from C in Mar 2018 with reference to its previous month?
questions.solution:

The rate of growth in sales from B in March 2018 with reference to its previous month = (9 – 7)/7 = 2/7

The rate of growth in sales from C in March 2018 with reference to its previous month = (8 – 5)/5 = 3/5

The ratio of rate of growth in sales from B to the rate of growth in sales from C in Mar 2018 with reference to its previous month = 2/7 : 3/5 = 10 : 21

**∴ The correct answer is 10 : 21.**

questions.question: Two items are sold for Rs. 18,602 each. On one item there has been a gain of 31% and on the second item a loss of 29%. What was the overall loss or gain in the transaction?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Two items are sold for Rs. 18,602 each

**Calculation:**

The cost price of the item sold at 31% gain = 18602 × 100/(100 + 31) = Rs. 14200

The cost price of the item sold at 29% loss = 18602 × 100/(100 – 29) = Rs. 26200

⇒ The total cost price of both the items = 14200 + 26200 = Rs. 40400

The total selling price of both the items = 18602 + 18602 = Rs. 37204

Loss = Total cost price – Total selling price

⇒ 40400 – 37204

⇒ Rs. 3196

Loss percent = (3196/40400) × 100 = 7.91%

**∴ The correct answer is 7.91%.**

questions.question: For θ being an acute angle, it is given that, 3 (cosec² θ + cot² θ) = 5. Then θ is equal to:
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

3 × (cosec² θ + cot² θ) = 5

⇒ 3( 1 + cot² θ + cot² θ ) = 5 (∵ cosec² θ – cot² θ = 1)

⇒ 3( 1 + 2 cot² θ) = 5

⇒ 3 + 6 cot² θ = 5

⇒ 6 cot² θ = 2

⇒ cot² θ = 2/6

⇒ cot² θ = 1/3

⇒ cot θ = 1/√3

⇒ θ = 60°

**∴ The correct answer is θ = 60°**

questions.question: The value of the expression (1)/(4)left{ {{{( {a + (1)/(a)} )}²} - {{( {a - (1)/(a)} )}²}} right} is:
The average of a number and its reciprocal is 4. The average of its cube and its reciprocal is equal to:
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Let the number be x.

The reciprocal of the number = 1/x

According to the question:

(x + 1/x)/2 = 4

⇒ x + 1/x = 8

⇒ (x + 1/x)³ = 512

⇒ x³ + 1/x³ + 3(x × 1/x)(x + 1/x) = 512

⇒ x³ + 1/x³ + 3(8) = 512

⇒ x³ + 1/x³ = 512 – 24

⇒ x³ + 1/x³ = 488

⇒ (x³ + 1/x³)/2 = 244

**∴ The average of cube of a number and its reciprocal is 244**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__****Concept used:**

x + 1/x = P

x3 + 1/x3 = P³ - 3P

**Calculation:**

Let the number be x.

The reciprocal of the number = 1/x

⇒ (x + 1/x)/2 = 4

⇒ x + 1/x = 8

⇒ x3 + 1/x3 = (8)³ - 3 × 8

⇒ x3 + 1/x3 = 512 - 24 = 488

The average of its cube and its reciprocal = 488/2 = 244

**∴ The correct answer is 244.**

questions.solution:
**Given:**

The seven-digit number 78x1y68 is divisible by 88.

**Concept used:**

(i) For a number to be divisible by 88, it should be divisible by 8 and 11.

(ii) **Divisibility Rule of 11:** For a number to be divisible by 11, the difference between the sum of digits at even places to the sum of digits at odd places should be zero or multiple of 11

**Calculations:**

Checking divisibility by 11,

⇒ The difference of (7 + x + y + 8) and (8 + 1 + 6) should be zero or multiple of 11.

(7 + x + y + 8) - (8 + 1 + 6) = 11

⇒ 15 + x + y – 15 = 11

⇒ x + y = 11

**∴ The value of (x + y) is 11.**

questions.question: If (3x + 1)³ + (x - 3)³ + (2x - 4)³ = 3 (3x + 1) (x - 3) (2x - 4), then x is equal to:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

(3x + 1)³ + (x - 3)³ + (2x - 4)³ = 3 (3x + 1) (x - 3) (2x - 4)

**Calculation:**

If a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc, then a + b + c = 0

So,

⇒ (3x + 1) + (x – 3) + (2x – 4) = 0

⇒ 6x – 6 = 0

⇒ 6x = 6

⇒ x = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

A certain sum invested on compound interest grows to Rs. 8,000 and Rs. 27,000 in three and six years, respectively when the interest is compounded annually, what is the percentage rate of interest?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Amount for 3 years = 8000

Amount for 6 years = 27000

**Formula used:**

A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

Where, A = Amount

P = Principal, r = Rate of interest, n = Time period

**Calculation:**

When the sum amounts to Rs.8000 in 3 years:

8000 = P(1 + r/100)³ ----(1)

When the sum amounts to Rs.27000 in 6 years:

27000 = P(1 + r/100)⁶ ----(2)

Dividing equation (2) by equation (1)

27/8 = (1 + r/100)³

Taking cube root on both the sides

1 + r/100 = 3/2

⇒ r/100 = 3/2 – 1

⇒ r/100 = 1/2

⇒ r = 50%

**∴ Rate of interest is 50% **

questions.question: If I travel by bus, I reach my office 15 min late, and if I travel by car, I reach 10 min early. If the distance between my home and my office is 25 km, then the difference of the reciprocals of average speeds of the bus and the car, in second per metre is:
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Difference in time = 15 + 10 = 25 min = 1500 second

Distance = 25 km = 25000 m

Let the speed of bus be B m/s and the speed of car be C m/s

⇒ 25000/B – 25000/C = 1500

⇒ 25000(1/B – 1/C) = 1500

⇒ 1/B – 1/C = 1500/25000 = 3/50

**∴ The difference of the reciprocals of average speeds of the bus and the car is 3/50 seconds per metre.**

questions.question: For an examination of a practical based subject, the total marks is 100. The break-up for theory, practical, project and viva voce is 40%, 30%, 20%, 10%. A candidate scored 80% in theory, 70% in practical, 60% in project and 50% in viva voce. What was her aggregate percentage?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Marks scored by the student in theory = 40 × 80/100 = 32

Marks scored by the student in practical = 30 × 70/100 = 21

Marks scored by the student in project = 20 × 60/100 = 12

Marks scored by the student in viva = 10 × 50/100 = 5

Total marks scored by the student = 32 + 21 + 12 + 5 = 70

The aggregate percentage = 70/100 × 100 = 70%

**∴ The correct answer is 70%**

questions.question: A savings fund in which both, the employer and the employee contribute regularly in the interest of the employee is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2) i.e. __Provident Fund__.**

__
 
• **Provident Fund__** is an amount of money consisting of regular payments by an employee and an employer over a period of time that the employee receives when they leave a company or retire.
 
• Employees' Provident Fund Organisation **(EPFO)** is the organisation which regulates the provident fund of all the workers employed in the Organised sector in India.
 
• A **mutual fund **is a company that pools money from many investors and invests the money in securities such as stocks, bonds, and short-term debt. 
 
• A **balanced fund** is a mutual fund that contains a stock component, a bond component and sometimes a money market component in a single portfolio.
 
• An **Index Fund** today is a source of investment for investors looking at the long term, less risky form of investment.

• It is used in a wide range of land assessment, management and planning efforts, including hazard assessment (including lava flows, landslides, tsunamis, and floods), forestry, agriculture, geologic mapping, and watershed and river surveys.

questions.question: Who among the following was appointed as the first Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1) i.e. __M. Ananthasayanam Ayyangar.__**

__
 
• **M. Ananthasayanam Ayyangar**__ served as the First Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
 
• He was born on 4 February 1891 at Tiruchanur near the spiritual town of Tirupati in Andhra Pradesh.
 
• After obtaining his B.A. degree from the Pachaiyappa's College, Madras, he earned a degree in Law from the Madras Law College in 1913
 
• He began his career as a Mathematics teacher in 1912. In 1915 he ventured into the legal profession- Within a short period, he established himself as a professional lawyer and, with his unusual ability to memorise cases, soon earned the reputation of being a 'walking digest of case laws'.
 
• Through a public life spanning over six decades as a lawyer, as a social activist and freedom fighter, as an outstanding parliamentarian and Speaker and as a distinguished scholar, Ayyangar left an indelible imprint of his personality in every area he chose to tread on in life.
